autonomy.execution_note: Five adaptive probes produced 25 scored answers and five warm-ups. A presence penalty left the selected six problems at 1/6. A frequency penalty rose from 1/6 to 2/6 there, then fell from 2/6 to 0/6 on additional practice counterparts; Astra rejected both leads. The paper grader agrees on all 25 answers. A separate live engineering test reproduced one published-edit response exactly, then verified further source editing and restores after feedback. No novel weight candidate or final submission was selected. Astra recommends the deferred BF16 control as the next measurement.
autonomy.summary: Astra can now choose practice problems and decoding settings, inspect generated answers, edit or restore a permitted source-weight snapshot, and test again while development stays open. Previously the fast browser path required final freeze. The new route prescribes no layer, edit strength, hypothesis or improvement threshold. Final evaluation still uses a frozen candidate.

findings: The published BF16 patch was reconstructed exactly: its complete shard hash matches the authors’ release. It changes 130,188 stored values in layers 15 and 19; the other 486 source tensors are unchanged. Under our original short, non-thinking settings, it scored 6/35 versus pristine 8/35, with 18 token-limit responses in each arm.

The grader does not explain the observed gap. The paper checker changes zero correctness labels on the earlier 1,000 saved MATH-500 outputs: the scores remain 97/500 and 98/500. It also agrees on all 112 responses from the completed published-edit controls.

Increasing the output ceiling from 1,024 to 3,072 left both arms at 1/7 on the matched seven problems. Truncations fell from 3 to 2 for pristine and 5 to 2 for the edit. The thinking controls remained heavily capped: all 14 responses in C and 13 of 14 in D reached 3,072 tokens. These short runs do not establish the published long-budget effect.

Quantization retains much of the published edit direction: delta cosines are 0.960 and 0.949, with directional gains 1.000 and 1.001 in layers 15 and 19. It also adds other changes. This geometry does not determine quantization’s accuracy effect.

We fixed repeated full-log parsing in the supervisor and recovery of partial streamed output. On the same saved log, mean idle polling fell from 9.039 to 0.0256 ms, while complete validation was retained. This measures monitoring work, not a model-speed or accuracy improvement.

grader_ablation.interpretation: Changes only extraction and mathematical checking on identical saved responses; does not test generation settings or weight edits.

limitations: WebLLM q4f16_1 differs from the paper’s BF16 vLLM. Quantization changes the deployed edit geometry: 296,905 decoded weights differ, including 208,739 outside the exact BF16 coordinates but within the affected 32-value groups. This proves the edit survives conversion; it does not establish an accuracy cost from quantization.
The browser API does not support top-k 20. Browser controls use one sample per problem and seed 42; the paper averages four samples at seed 0.

A’s seven-problem row reuses saved responses from its 35-problem run. It is not a new independent run. The prospective reduction of later stages to the preselected seven IDs bounds local runtime and is recorded before those stages produce outputs.

Completed A–D stages retain every scheduled scored response. The incomplete E attempts do not supply accuracy estimates. Truncated answers may receive credit when their extracted final answer is correct. Paper-checker grades remain a separately reported analysis and do not overwrite primary browser grades.
Response seconds exclude model loading and warm-up. Shorter output alone does not establish lower per-token compute, physical memory or energy.
The exact original CUDA runtime package and hardware manifest was not published. Matching the released protocol would not establish bit-for-bit runtime reproduction.

B uses qualified offline reports after an obsolete post-run validator rejected outputs above 1,024 tokens. Its actual declared ceiling was 3,072. Both original reports and global failure flags remain preserved; the same correction checks both arms and changes no generated answers, primary grades or accuracy counts.

Development compute is also unmatched. The study offered 7,469 GSM8K and 7,275 MATH training problems and up to 512 answers per budgeted generation pass. Our open research probes used a 70-problem MATH pool and produced 25 new scored answers; the separately reported controls add further diagnostic feedback. A shared nominal allowance of 50 forward attempts does not imply comparable model work.

C changes the prompt/template and thinking mode together; D changes temperature, top-p and presence penalty together. E also expands context along with the output ceiling. These stages do not isolate every individual setting.

The first long-control attempt was interrupted for an operational monitoring defect, before any scored response completed. Its warm-up, failed dispatch and partial output remain recorded, with unknown observed scored tokens/time. The new E condition also changes context from that attempt’s 65,536 to the paper’s 34,816; monitoring and context effects are not separately identified by the restarted model run.

The expected EOS token IDs agree across released tokenizer/config metadata and the inspected vLLM behavior. Browser literal stop-string handling, special-token decoding and primary answer extraction still have edge differences. Independent paper-checker replay reports the observed label effects separately; matching IDs alone does not prove identical original runtime behavior.

The browser development route selects from its prepared 70 training problems; custom practice prompts remain available through the CPU diagnostic route. Weight editing retains the paper’s internal-block scope and prohibition on whole-tensor scalar-only changes. These scope rules do not select a layer, hypothesis, strength or required improvement.

Both long attempts retain incomplete scored requests. Observed scored-token counts and response durations are unknown; conservative ledger charges are not measurements. Process exit was verified after forced termination, while graceful model unload was not confirmed. The E-v3 recovery retained 62,280 characters; only the first D baseline prefix could be checked, and the other thirteen planned comparisons remain unexecuted.

published_edit.label: Published p50c
published_edit.summary: Exact source reconstruction followed by independently audited q4f16_1 deployment.

reference_execution.summary: The exact published edit and portable BF16/vLLM reference bundle are prepared. CPU preflight checks pass for all 500 prompt templates and reference answers. The released protocol uses thinking, 32,768 output tokens, a 34,816-token context, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, presence penalty 1.5, seed 0 and four averaged samples per problem. A separate 16-response training-only pilot is prepared for checking runtime fit and cost. CUDA execution is deferred because no GPU host is available. Neither the CUDA smoke, pilot nor full reference run has executed.

scope: These are diagnostics on MATH training problems disjoint from the MATH-500 test set. They do not supply a new MATH-500 score. The completed 500-problem fresh-edit experiment remains below. Completed seven-problem conditions reuse the same IDs selected in advance, one per subject; their percentages are coarse practice observations.

summary: The earlier 500-problem run used a fresh edit, disabled thinking and a 1,024-position ceiling. We tested the published edit under progressively closer settings and opened Astra’s research loop. Short controls are complete; the 32,768-token local control timed out before producing a paired score.
